primitives.name: Perceiver-style Temporal Aggregator
primitives.verbatim_quote: MatchVoice generator: frozen visual encoder (C3D/ResNet/CLIP/InternVideo/Baidu) → 2-layer Perceiver-style temporal aggregator (32 learnable queries) → MLP projection to 768-d prefix tokens → LLaMA-3 decoder (frozen or LoRA rank 8–64), standard NLL loss, 30-s input window.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'encoder': 'Pre-trained visual backbone (output dimension varies)', 'num_queries': 'Number of learnable temporal queries (32)', 'decoder_rank': 'Low-rank adaptation rank (8, 16, 32, 64)', 'input_window': 'Temporal receptive field (30 seconds)', 'prefix_dim': 'Dimensionality of projected token sequence (768)'}
primitives.assumptions: Local 30-s context suffices for accurate commentary generation; frozen encoders capture sufficient visual semantics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting occurs when LoRA ranks exceed encoder capacity (~768 dimensions), leading to catastrophic forgetting.

primitives.name: Coarse-to-Fine Alignment Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question Soccer commentary datasets (SoccerNet-Caption, 471 matches) suffer large text↔video timestamp misalignments that corrupt commentary-generation training; can a two-stage (ASR+LLM coarse → CLIP-contrastive fine) alignment pipeline repair them, and does training on the aligned dataset (MatchTime) produce a state-of-the-art commentary generator (MatchVoice)?
primitives.assumptions: ASR transcripts provide initial coarse alignment; contrastive learning on CLIP embeddings refines it; the combined pipeline converges to ground-truth timestamps.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Pipeline failure occurs when ASR errors compound, requiring robust filtering.

The core challenge is aligning noisy, broadcast-as-recorded timestamps with true event times. The affinity-based alignment maps to a maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) estimation under a multinomial softmax likelihood, where the prior favors temporal coherence. This is mathematically equivalent to a differentiable ArgMax operation, which is a fundamental building block for GSI's sequential anomaly detection and GSE's discrete-event state machines. The Perceiver aggregator acts as a low-rank bilinear pooling kernel, compressing high-dimensional visual streams into a fixed-size query space, mirroring GSI's Kalman filters and GSE's recurrent memory units. The coarse-to-fine pipeline implements a hierarchical hypothesis test: first, a fast, approximate test (ASR) is used to prune implausible hypotheses; then, a slower, more accurate test (CLIP contrastive) confirms the most likely one. This dual-threshold approach prevents false alarms while maintaining statistical power. The MatchTime dataset corrects systematic biases by iteratively re-weighting misaligned pairs, akin to GSI's importance sampling and GSE's state-dependent transition kernels. Failure modes arise when the softmax temperature becomes too sharp, causing sensitivity to noise, or too flat, causing oversmoothing. To avoid leakage, the alignment must be performed before any downstream generation, ensuring that the generator never sees corrupted labels. Empirically, the pipeline reduces mean absolute error from 16.63s to 6.89s, demonstrating robustness to replay edits and camera cuts.
